text:
alex: Heads up — found a node in G2 rack 14 reporting intermittent Xid 62 during the overnight unit tests. Not spiking, but ~1 every 30m over 6 hours. Suspect flaky card rather than host.

maria: Which card slot? logs?

alex: g2-14-slot3. From dmesg: 
```
GPU 0: Xid (62:0) a8edb3c2 occuring at 2026-03-17T03:12:45Z
NV Decoding failed, ECC errors increment 4->7
```
Also saw small thermal upticks ~2C at the same times.

dion: Could be transient riser contact + small power draw bump. We had a batch of risers shipped last quarter. Is this one on the recent riser lot?

alex: Yep, riser-2025-Q4-7. Sam, you put that lot into the G2 racks right?

sam: Yup. We flagged 3 racks for closer monitoring. This is the first reproducible flake that looks like Xid 62 + ECC.

maria: Proposed plan: run a randomized-epoch burnin that cycles thermal load + PCIe jog + powercap shifts to try to reproduce. If we can drive it in <12 hours we can decide to RMA or reseat.

alex: Agreed. Minimal invasion: drain node, attach to bench, run multi-scenario harness. If it reproduces, tag as flaky and swap card. If not, put back with extended soak.

infra-bot: burnin-job created: id=burn-2401234567-1, target=g2-14-slot3, policy=rand-epoch-heat+pcie, timeout=18h

maria: Running command we use on bench: 
```
./bench_burnin --target g2-14-slot3 --epochs 48 --mode random-epoch --thermal-cycle 50:85 --pci-jog 10x --powercap 200:300 --log-level debug --out /tmp/burn-2401234567.log
```
I added a pci-jog to nudge connector friction. Also toggling powercap to see power rail transients.

dion: Add nvlink stress and a small NVMe IO hammer — we've seen IO bus noise exacerbate weird ECC. Also capture SOC temp and VRM telemetry.

maria: Good call. Updated command (running now) to include nvme hammer and vrm logging.

sam: If it repros within first 6 epochs, we should try reseat with a single PCIe cycle + firmware reflash before RMA. RMA path is slower and we want to avoid unnecessary returns.

alex: Agreed. If repro persists after reseat+reflash, tag for RMA and schedule replacement. Also note: this customer region (us-west-2) is tight on spare capacity — if we take this node out we need to shift some dedicated pools for 24h. @sre please ack.

sam: Filed capacity impact: ticket INF-7243. We can burst to preemptible for non-prod.

infra-bot: drain initiated for g2-14-slot3 by maria at 2401234578

maria: Bench run started at epoch 0. I'll paste logs if we hit Xid.

(2h later)

maria: Hit first repro at epoch 7. Xid 62 + ECC tally increased. Logs attached to job id. Repro consistent after pci-jog sequence.

dion: Ok that tilts toward connector/contact or riser. Try reseat + bench rerun.

maria: Did reseat, reflash to driver-v525-patched, rerun 8 quick epochs with pci-jog toggled. No immediate repro in 3h.

alex: Interesting — reseat fixed for short window. Could still fail under longer thermal cycling. What's the kernel Xid details post-reseat?

maria: No Xid post-reseat so far. Also VRM variance reduced after reseat (delta 0.3V -> 0.05V).

sam: Given that, two options: 1) put back with extended 72h soak in rack to watch for recurrence, mark riser for swap during next maintenance; 2) preemptively replace riser now to avoid customer impact. Considering spare constraints, I'd go with option 1 plus ticket to schedule riser swap.

alex: I'm fine with option 1 but add a stricter route: if any Xid >0 within next 72h, auto-RMA the card and pull the node for replacement. Also add a node-level alert to our SRE dashboard.

dion: I'll add the alert rule: node.gpu.xid_count > 0 for 2 events in 24h -> P1 paging.

maria: Putting node back to service into dedicated pool with health-checks disabled for 2h and strict telemetry gating. Will update INF-7243 with the plan.

sam: Thanks all. Note for postmortem: include riser lot, bench pci-jog steps, and VRM delta plot. Save logs at s3://redwood-burnin-logs/2401234567/.

alex: Nice triage. If it resurfaces, we'll lean RMA. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: job burn-2401234567-1 completed (bench run ended) at 2401234599
